question.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 5 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $u\,⊥\,v.$ Find $(v+w)\cdot u+v\cdot (u+w).$

current_example.problem: Let ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14268503/assets/c9815448eb5267ed8dc5daff548b6620f57f0e99c6ce1065cd6b538878d12839.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14268503/assets/14d439585eb7df58b2f03cf7b0f8a2309540816df157923e06a7d59c90884252.svg) be vectors such that $\mathbf{u} \!\perp\! \mathbf{w}$. Find $(\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{v})\cdot \mathbf{w} + \mathbf{u}\cdot(\mathbf{v}+ \mathbf{w}).$
current_example.worked_solution:
Since $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{w}$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that $\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{w}=0$. Therefore, using linearity of the dot product to expand the parentheses, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(u+v)\cdot w+u\cdot (v+w) & =u\cdot w+v\cdot w+u\cdot v+u\cdot w \\  & =0+v\cdot w+u\cdot v+0 \\  & =v\cdot w+u\cdot v \\  & =(2\cdot (-1)+(-3)\cdot 3+4\cdot 1) \\  & +((-1)\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-3)+5\cdot 4)\, \\  & =(-2-9+4)+(-2+6+20) \\  & =-7+24 \\  & =17.\end{aligned}
$$
